To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated the growth of silicon quantum dots in different dielectric matrixes.
Si QD embedded in SiO2 matrix shows a blue shifted emission, which is attributed to quantum confinement effect and the emission can be tuned by varying the Si concentration and the Si QD diameter.

we can produce silicon quantum dots with a size distribution of 2 to 5 nm in diameter and that the bandgap can be opened up to 2.2 eV, which is a significant improvement over the 1.1 eV bandgap of bulk Si.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth and characterization of Si quantum dots, and their use in tandem cells.
the development of a wide bandgap material for silicon tandem solar cells, based on silicon quantum dots embedded in dielectric matrix.
developing a novel approach for the design and growth of a new class of materials, which can be utilized for the development of silicon tandem cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Si quantum dots in a dielectric matrix can be used for tandem solar cells.
the bandgap opening of Si quantum dots is strongly dependent on the dielectric matrix.
the Si quantum dots in nitride are the best candidate for the tandem cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Si QDs in SiN matrix have the best potential for photovoltaic application.
the bandgap opening of Si quantum dots can be achieved in different matrices.
the Si QDs in SiC, SiN, SiO2 matrixes were fabricated, the bandgap of Si QDs was tuned by the matrix, the PL lifetime was also tuned.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Si QDs in a dielectric matrix are a viable route to a silicon based tandem photovoltaic material.
the bandgap opening of silicon quantum dots can be controlled by the matrix material.
we have demonstrated that the quantum confinement in Si can be used to engineer wide bandgap materials for tandem solar cells.
